backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Keep a safe copy of your mail, contacts, and settings. Set backups up before you store real data.
backups.honestyNote: Owlat can't read your server's schedule from here, so this page tracks the plan {you} record. Run the commands shown on your server, then note here what you set up — that's how the app knows your data is protected.
backups.noPlanDescription: Nothing here is protected until you schedule backups on your server. Follow the steps below, then record what you set up.
backups.dailyScheduleDescription: Runs a backup every night. Enable it on your server, then flip this switch to record it.
backups.backUpNowDescription: Run this on your server for an immediate backup, then log the result here.
backups.restoreDescription: Backups are written to {path} on your server. To restore one, run:
backups.sealedMailTitle: Sealed Mail and your instance secret
backups.sealedMailBody: Mail that arrives sealed is stored encrypted. The only things that can open it again are your instance secret ({secret}) and the recovery kits you download from Sealed Mail settings.
backups.sealedMailWarning: If you lose the instance secret and haven't kept any recovery kits, sealed mail you already received can no longer be opened, and a database backup alone will not bring it back. Keep the instance secret in your backups, and download a recovery kit for each address before you rely on Sealed Mail.
backups.restoreWarning: Restoring replaces current data with the snapshot — stop the stack and confirm the tarball before running it in production.
